methods.label: Compare corresponding decimal places
methods.explanation:
Write \(2.005\) as \(2.0050\) so both numbers show the same decimal places. In \(2.00d5\), the digit \(d\) is in the thousandths place.

If \(d\) is \(0,1,2,3,\) or \(4\), that place is smaller than the corresponding \(5\), so the inequality fails. If \(d=5\), then \(2.0055>2.0050\) because of the final decimal place. If \(d\) is \(6,7,8,\) or \(9\), the thousandths place already makes the number larger.

Thus the successful digits are \(5,6,7,8,9\), exactly \(\boxed{5}\) values, choice \(\text{C}\).
